inputs.text: France’s conviction of Father Bernard Domini under the new law on “psychological subjection” highlights the power imbalance that can leave people vulnerable to coercive authority. Religious freedom should protect belief, not give powerful institutions immunity from accountability. The state must not control conscience either: protections need clear, fair standards and safeguards against unchecked official power. The focus should be on whether people are being harmed, and on holding institutions accountable without targeting faith itself.
